card: Enforces explicit range checking on numeric startup options rather than allowing negative or out-of-bounds values to silently wrap, overflow, or invert time offsets. Options validated include -dbbatchsize, -maxtipage, mempool cluster limits, buffer sizes, timeouts, and wallet fee confirmation targets. The author notes that a negative -dbbatchsize wrapped into an immense uint64_t and disabled database flushing during reindex, while an out-of-range -txconfirmtarget silently forced all wallet transactions onto fallback fee rates.
changed_since_previous: Added validation for -txconfirmtarget in the wallet (checking bounds against unsigned int and the fee estimator's maximum target blocks) along with functional test coverage in wallet_fallbackfee.py.
evidence: PR description and commit: "A negative -dbbatchsize wrapped to a huge value and disabled batch flushing, so a reindex could hold an unbounded batch in memory."

Source comments in src/node/chainstatemanager_args.cpp and src/wallet/wallet.cpp note that negative -maxtipage puts the IBD cutoff in the future, and out-of-range -txconfirmtarget silently forces every transaction to fall back to -fallbackfee.
problem: Passing negative or out-of-bounds values to numeric options silently wraps or overflows when narrowed into unsigned or smaller types, and can invert time calculations. For example, a negative -dbbatchsize wraps to an enormous uint64_t that disables batch flushing and risks unbounded memory growth during reindex, negative -maxtipage keeps a node permanently stuck in initial block download, and out-of-range -txconfirmtarget causes fee estimation to fail and silently fall back to -fallbackfee for all transactions.

risk.why: Faulty bounds checking or unexpected rejection of existing edge-case configuration values could prevent nodes or wallets from starting up.

summary: Enforces bounds checking on numeric configuration arguments across node startup, validation, mempool, networking, and wallet initialization. Arguments that previously accepted negative or out-of-range numbers (such as -dbbatchsize, -maxtipage, mempool cluster limits, buffer sizes, -timeout, and -txconfirmtarget) now raise initialization errors instead of wrapping when narrowed to unsigned types, inverting time cutoffs, or silently falling back. The change also updates -help text for several options to document their =<n> value placeholders.
